- Largest manufacturer of contact and non-contact temperature sensors in India by revenue as of March 31, 2026 with approximately 10.5% temperature-sensor market share in Fiscal 2026, and the only Indian manufacturer of non-contact temperature sensors with approximately 21.3% share (Source: F&S Report - commissioned industry report, not the issuer's own market data)

- Diversified business model with three verticals, wide industry coverage and a balanced mix of Project/OEM (67.55% of Fiscal 2026 revenue excluding other operating revenue) and recurring MRO revenue (32.45%)
- Make-to-order engineering with approval-driven entry barriers - extended qualification periods, in-depth testing and field trials before supplier approval, supporting customer retention and cross-selling

- Global presence through subsidiaries and joint ventures in India, UAE, Germany, Poland, Indonesia and South Korea, exports to more than 80 countries between April 1, 2023 and March 31, 2026, and 28 distributors as of March 31, 2026

bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Dependence on Projects/OEM business — Projects/OEM contributed 67.55%, 69.16% and 63.99% of revenue from operations (excluding scrap sale and export incentive) in Fiscals 2026, 2025 and 2024. These are large, sometimes one-time orders with long sales cycles whose timing and volume move with customer capital expenditure cycles.
- End-user industry concentration in metals and petrochemicals — Metal and petrochemical industries collectively contributed 41.13%, 42.90% and 41.52% of revenue from operations in Fiscals 2026, 2025 and 2024; a downturn in these cyclical sectors would directly reduce demand.
- Working capital intensity — Net Working Capital Days rose to 210 in Fiscal 2026 from 193 in Fiscal 2025 and 152 in Fiscal 2024 on higher inventory from customisation and dispatch clearance delays, tying up cash and increasing reliance on borrowings as the business scales.
- Raw material price volatility and import dependence — Inputs include copper, aluminium, stainless steel, nickel alloys, platinum and rhodium; ₹512.04 million or 19.64% of Fiscal 2026 purchases were sourced outside India, exposing costs to commodity prices, logistics, tariffs and currency movements.
- Acquisition-driven growth and non-comparable financials — Fiscal 2026 reflects the Tempsens GmbH, Tempsens Polska and Tempsens Measurement acquisitions and Fiscal 2025 the Marathon Heater amalgamation, which created goodwill of ₹1,061.28 million; management states the years are not directly comparable and reported ROE is depressed by the resulting goodwill and intangibles.
- Joint venture and overseas subsidiary control limitations — Key actions in the joint ventures require majority, unanimous or partner consent, and in the JVs and the overseas subsidiary the chief executive or a board member is often a shareholder or a shareholder's relative, complicating incentives and enforcement; control of Tempsens Instruments GmbH rests on a governance agreement over a 50.00% stake.
- Export and international expansion exposure — Revenue from outside India was 28.52%, 26.70% and 21.49% of revenue (excluding other operating revenue) in Fiscals 2026, 2025 and 2024, exposing the business to currency movements, trade restrictions and local regulation, and to the risk that new markets such as Mexico do not scale.
- Low utilisation of newly added capacity — Electrical heating installed capacity jumped to 317,400 units in Fiscal 2025 from 2,200 in Fiscal 2024, yet vertical utilisation was 54.75% in Fiscal 2026 (Unit VI at 41.35%) and conductor capacity ran at 55.75%, so further capex must be absorbed before it earns a return.

business.body: Tempsens designs and manufactures customised temperature sensing solutions, electrical heating solutions and specialised cables for industrial process applications. Products are made-to-order for end users in metals, petrochemicals, power, defence and nuclear, glass, plastics and manufacturing, sold both as high-barrier Project/OEM supply (67.55% of Fiscal 2026 revenue from operations excluding other operating revenue) and as recurring MRO replacement business (32.45%). It served more than 1,000 unique customers between April 1, 2023 and March 31, 2026 and exported to more than 80 countries over the same period.

outlook.body:
- Expand and commercialise new products by leveraging R&D capabilities and technological partnerships - developing specialised thermocouples, mid-voltage heaters and a new line of high-precision infrared pyrometers and online thermal imagers
- Prioritise solutions for emerging industries - battery energy storage systems, decarbonisation, fuel cells, green hydrogen, advanced exhaust heating for automotive emission control, defence and aerospace, metal recycling and nuclear power
- Scale established product lines - process heating, nickel alloy conductor solutions and infrared technology - by expanding production capacity, automating key manufacturing processes and strengthening global distribution and after-sales engineering support
- Maintain and expand global presence and export sales - enter Europe, the Middle East, North America and South America, register with major end users, EPC companies and OEMs, and invest in international certifications for products and facilities
- Continue growth through organic and inorganic initiatives, including mergers, acquisitions, alliances, new joint ventures and subsidiaries, pursuing consolidation of fragmented target markets at attractive valuations
- Continue to focus on improving operational efficiency and expanding manufacturing capacity - process optimisation, automation and digital systems, energy-efficient practices, proposed expansion of Unit VI, and additional land procured for future expansion
- Deepen backward integration to control critical inputs, optimise raw material utilisation and reduce reliance on external suppliers
- Expand the replacement (MRO) business and diversify industry presence across metals, petrochemicals, defence and nuclear, manufacturing, power, trading, glass and plastics to drive resilient, annuity-style growth
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: Growth is pursued on three fronts. First, brownfield capacity at Udaipur: the Net Proceeds fund plant, machinery and equipment for the electrical heating solutions vertical at Unit VI and the specialised cable solutions vertical at Unit IV, plus civil and building work for sheds and related infrastructure on existing vacant land within the Unit VI premises, so the machinery goes into existing sites rather than a new location. Following the proposed capital expenditure, electrical heating installed capacity rises from 317,400 units to 341,400 units (+7.56%) and specialised cable capacity from 10,200 kilometres to 11,400 kilometres (+11.76%), with nickel alloy conductor capacity unchanged at 400 metric tons; management has also procured additional land on which further expansion may be envisaged. Second, inorganic and partnership-led expansion: the Marathon Heater amalgamation (effective March 6, 2025, appointed date April 1, 2024), the acquisitions of Tempsens Instruments GmbH and Tempsens Polska (effective January 16, 2026) and of Tempsens Measurement and Control (March 30, 2026), plus technology joint ventures such as Pyrosens with Micro-Epsilon and Victura Tempsens for automotive cables. Third, geographic expansion: 15 manufacturing units worldwide including Joint Ventures (ten in Udaipur, five overseas in the UAE, South Korea, Indonesia, Germany and Poland), a sales presence being established in Mexico where the entity is registered but capital infusion is still ongoing, and a stated push into Europe, the Middle East, North America and South America backed by continued investment in international product and facility certifications.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Revenue from operations grew 17.53% to ₹4,448.78 million in Fiscal 2026, led by electrical heating solutions (+44.89%) on major order execution and deeper penetration in industrial and renewables segments, with temperature sensing +12.73% and specialised cables +11.06%
- Mix shift toward electrical heating, which was 20.70% of Fiscal 2026 vertical revenue versus 3.90% in Fiscal 2024, following the Marathon Heater amalgamation and operationalisation of Unit VI
- Export-led growth - revenue from outside India rose to ₹1,258.21 million (28.52% of revenue excluding other operating revenue) in Fiscal 2026 from ₹586.36 million (21.49%) in Fiscal 2024, a stated 46.49% CAGR between Fiscals 2024 and 2026
- Working capital cycle lengthening - Net Working Capital Days rose to 210 in Fiscal 2026 from 193 in Fiscal 2025 and 152 in Fiscal 2024, primarily on higher inventory holding from customisation requirements, dispatch clearance delays and the Marathon Heater amalgamation
- Input cost and volume effect - cost of material consumed rose 25.14% to ₹2,484.25 million on higher production volumes and higher commodity input costs, against a 17.53% revenue increase; total expenses rose 20.42% to ₹3,640.39 million
- Inventory build of ₹83.27 million credited to the statement of profit and loss in Fiscal 2026 as stock was raised to support anticipated demand after capacity expansions
- Other income rose 178.46% to ₹109.77 million on interest income from higher fixed deposit balances (₹47.98 million) and net foreign exchange gains (₹34.83 million)
- Contract liabilities (customer advances) increased to ₹119.94 million as at March 31, 2026 from ₹70.42 million a year earlier, which management describes as indicating a growing order book
- Reported profitability is not comparable across years - Fiscal 2026 reflects the GmbH, Polska and Tempsens Measurement acquisitions and Fiscal 2025 the Marathon Heater amalgamation, so the Company also presents Adjusted PAT and Adjusted ROE excluding Ind AS 103 intangible amortisation and goodwill (Adjusted ROE 20.70% versus reported ROE 13.54% in Fiscal 2026)
- R&D expense stepped up to ₹11.62 million in Fiscal 2026 from ₹5.07 million in Fiscal 2025

order_book.coverage_note: NO order-book value is disclosed anywhere in this RHP. The document contains no 'orders in hand', 'outstanding orders', 'unexecuted orders' or 'backlog' figure (zero occurrences of 'backlog'); the only reference to an order book is qualitative, in the MD&A: 'Advances from customers (recorded as contract liabilities) increased to Rs 119.94 million as at March 31, 2026, from Rs 70.42 million as at March 31, 2025, indicating a growing order book and stronger customer commitment.' Advances from customers are a balance-sheet contract liability, NOT an order book, and are recorded here only as the sole quantified forward-commitment proxy the RHP prints. This is a SILENCE on the order book, not an affirmative nil. The Company describes itself as make-to-order with 67.55% of Fiscal 2026 revenue from Projects/OEM orders, so an order book plausibly exists but is not quantified.

business_ops.supply_chain_integration: Heavily backward-integrated manufacture. 'We are among the very few companies in the world with a backward-integrated manufacturing facility for thermocouples, cables, and electrical heaters, located at Udaipur, India, as of March 31, 2026 (Source: F&S Report).' Key in-house capabilities now include alloy melting, hot-rolling, annealing, mineral-insulated cable manufacturing, machining, final assembly and calibration: 'Previously, we relied on external suppliers for most metallurgical finished goods, but by internalising these critical steps, we have reduced our dependence on third parties.' For heater products the Company manufactures heating alloys, produces tubular heating elements, fabricates vessels and performs final assembly including instrumentation, process connections and panel integration entirely in-house, and also produces the thermocouple conductor used in thermocouple cables - stated to have 'increased operational control, enhanced product consistency, and allowed us to shorten lead times'. Certain units manufacture products used as raw materials by other units as well as being supplied to external customers. New products are frequently used internally before external launch (thermowells, thermocouple cables, mineral-insulated and specialised cables, thermocouple and heating-alloy nickel-based conductors). Indigenisation is framed under 'Make in India': thermocouple and heating conductors previously imported are now manufactured in-house, and the Company states it has 'reduced reliance on foreign suppliers' by indigenising non-contact temperature sensor development. Manufacturing is make-to-order: 'Each manufacturing job operates on a make-to-order basis, i.e., customer requirements are translated into detailed engineering and design workflows, resulting in precise production drawings.' INPUTS: metals and alloys (platinum, nickel, stainless steel, copper, inconel), insulating materials (magnesium oxide, ceramics, fibreglass, PTFE), coatings (silicone, PVC, polyimide). Cost of materials procured from India was Rs 2,095.61 / 1,681.12 / 1,419.40 million and from outside India Rs 512.04 / 408.29 / 235.76 million for Fiscals 2026 / 2025 / 2024, i.e. 80.36% / 80.46% / 85.76% domestic and 19.64% / 19.54% / 14.24% imported; purchases during the year were Rs 2,607.65 / 2,089.41 / 1,655.16 million (71.63% / 69.12% / 72.88% of total expenses) and cost of materials consumed Rs 2,484.25 / 1,985.13 / 1,717.06 million (68.24% / 65.67% / 75.60% of total expenses). Suppliers span 18 Indian states and two union territories and 18 foreign countries (including China, USA, UK, Singapore, Germany, Israel, France, Austria, Czech Republic, Japan, South Korea, Indonesia, UAE, Thailand, Canada, Taiwan and Hong Kong). FORWARD/OUTBOUND: no owned logistics - 'We rely on third-party logistics providers ... We do not operate our own logistics fleet, nor do we conduct logistics operations through related party transactions. We rely on spot-based arrangements with third-party logistics providers, utilising air, road, and rail transportation modes.' R&D is conducted entirely in-house with a dedicated team of 83 employees as of March 31, 2026 (10.20% of total group headcount of 814); granted IP comprises 12 patents in India, eight registered trademarks in India, one copyright registration in India and 39 trademark registrations outside India, with one patent, four Indian trademarks and three foreign trademarks pending. Working capital: Net Working Capital Days of 210 / 193 / 152 for Fiscals 2026 / 2025 / 2024 (days sales outstanding plus days inventory outstanding minus days payable outstanding), the increase 'primarily attributable to a higher inventory holding resulting from customization requirements, delays in dispatch clearance, and the impact of the amalgamation of Marathon Heater ... acquisition of Tempsens GmbH, Tempsens Polaska and Tempsens Measurement and Control Private Limited'.

The 10.5% share is the temperature sensor segment (India temperature sensor and allied products market estimated at INR 18.8 billion in FY26); the separate 21.3% figure is the non-contact temperature sensor sub-segment. No group-level / consolidated market share is stated for electrical heating solutions or specialised cables - for heaters the RHP states only 'one of the largest manufacturers of electrical heaters in India' and 'one of the leading players in electric heaters as of March 31, 2026, particularly process heaters', with no percentage.

opportunities: Expanding and commercialising new products by leveraging R&D capabilities and technological partnerships, including specialised thermocouples, mid-voltage heaters, and a new line of high-precision infrared pyrometers and online thermal imagers; the Pyrosens partnership with Micro-Epsilon covers pyrometers and online thermal imagers with all manufacturing being shifted to India.
Scaling established product lines - process heating, conductor solutions and infrared technology - with planned production capacity expansion and automation of key manufacturing processes.

Maintaining and expanding global presence and export sales, targeting Europe, the Middle East, North America and South America, and pursuing long-term contracts by registering with major end users, EPC companies and original equipment manufacturers.

Growth through organic and inorganic initiatives including joint ventures and subsidiaries; consolidation of fragmented target markets at attractive valuations; acquisition and partnership opportunities under evaluation in Saudi Arabia, the United States and Brazil, with no definitive agreements finalised as at the date of the RHP.

Indigenisation trend in India's sensor and heater industries, with leading players working with government and industrial partners in steel, power, defence and other process-intensive sectors to develop and manufacture advanced sensors, furnace cameras and heating solutions domestically (Source: F&S Report).

Emerging end markets prioritised by the Company: battery energy storage systems, decarbonization, fuel cells, green hydrogen and ammonia manufacturing, advanced exhaust heating for automotive emission control, defence and aerospace, space, metal recycling, thermal storage and nuclear power.

Indian non-contact temperature sensors, currently holding an 11.8% share, are projected to grow at a CAGR of 11-12% from FY2026 to FY2031 versus a 7-8% CAGR for contact sensors (69.4% share) over the same period (Source: F&S Report).
strengths: Largest manufacturer of contact and non-contact temperature sensors in India in terms of revenue and one of the largest manufacturers of electrical heaters in India (Source: F&S Report), with a focus on indigenisation resulting in high entry barriers (qualitative factor stated in Basis for Offer Price).
Only Indian manufacturer of non-contact temperature sensors as of March 31, 2026, holding approximately 21.3% of that sub-segment in Fiscal 2026 (Source: F&S Report).
Diversified business model with broad product portfolio, wide industry coverage, and balanced mix of projects and MRO revenue (qualitative factor stated in Basis for Offer Price).

Established research and development capabilities enabling customized, critical solutions and innovation; R&D team of 83 dedicated employees as at March 31, 2026, total R&D spend for FY2026 of INR 55.54 million, and 11 patents held by Tempsens and its subsidiaries.

Global presence through strategic alliances, diverse customer base, export sales and strong long-standing customer relationships; products delivered to customers in more than 80 countries; 15 manufacturing units (10 in Udaipur, India; 5 overseas in UAE, South Korea, Indonesia, Germany and Poland).

Integrated global operations featuring backward integration, digital traceability, and stringent quality control; certifications include ISO 9001:2015, ISO 14001:2015, ISO 45001:2018, an ISO/IEC 17025:2017 accredited calibration laboratory in Udaipur, and product approvals such as ATEX, IECEx, UL, CE, EAC, BIS, U Stamp, R Stamp and PESO.

High entry barriers from strict product registration and certification criteria, extended supplier qualification periods, in-depth testing and comprehensive field trials before approval for mission-critical applications (Source: F&S Report), fostering customer loyalty and cross-selling opportunities.

Operations led by the Promoters (Virendra Prakash Rathi, Vinay Rathi, Pratap Singh Talesara) and supported by an experienced management team; many KMPs and Senior Management associated with the Company for an average of 15 years each as of March 31, 2026.
threats: Highly competitive industry across all three verticals. Key competitors in temperature sensors and allied products in India: Pyro Electric, Precision Mass Products and Radix Electrosystems; major global competitors serving the Indian market: Endress+Hauser, WIKA Instruments, OMEGA Engineering and Honeywell. Key global suppliers into the Indian heating solutions market: Thermon Inc., Heat Trace Limited, Alleima (Kanthal), Zoppas Industries, nVent Thermal, Heatwell, Hotset GmbH and IRCA S.p.A. Specialised cables competitors: Thermo Cables Limited and Thermon India Private Limited (Source: F&S Report).

Global multinationals in temperature sensing invest heavily in technological innovation and digitalisation, commanding strong brand recognition and influencing advanced industry sectors, presenting challenges in keeping pace with innovation and market expectations.

Demand concentration in metal and petrochemical end-user industries, which collectively contributed 41.13%, 42.90% and 41.52% of revenue from operations (excluding scrap sale and export incentive) for Fiscals 2026, 2025 and 2024.

Volatility, increases, fluctuations, shortages or delays in the supply of primary raw materials; key materials such as nickel, chromium, stainless steel and special alloys used in heating elements are prone to global price swings (Source: F&S Report).

Competition from low-cost alternatives - domestic manufacturers face pricing pressure from unorganised players offering cheaper, low-spec heaters and furnaces, eroding margins for quality-focused companies and discouraging investment in R&D (Source: F&S Report).

Export exposure - 28.52%, 26.70% and 21.49% of revenue (excluding other operating revenue) came from outside India for Fiscals 2026, 2025 and 2024; any reduction in demand or loss of business from export markets may adversely impact results.

Dependence on imported components - specialised heating elements, temperature sensors and control modules are still imported from Europe, Japan and China, exposing the industry to supply chain disruptions such as freight rate spikes and geopolitical tensions (Source: F&S Report).

Business operations involve dealings with government entities, including in sensitive sectors such as defence and space; any delay, modification, cancellation or adverse change in government policies, procurement processes, contract terms or regulatory requirements could materially and adversely affect results.
Growth is dependent on industry capex trends and timely execution of new product launches and developments, with no assurance that recent consistent growth will be sustained.
High upfront costs and long payback periods for industrial heaters, furnaces and advanced electric heating systems deter adoption by MSMEs and cost-sensitive industries (Source: F&S Report).
weaknesses: No exact comparable listed peers in India or internationally, which the RHP itself flags as a risk: valuation of the Company compared with other listed players in India may not be comparable and could be higher on account of certain aspects (Risk Factor 55).

Financial and operational results for Fiscal 2026 and Fiscal 2025 are not directly comparable with previous periods, reflecting the acquisition of Tempsens Instruments GmbH and Tempsens Polska sp. z o.o. in Fiscal 2026 and the amalgamation of Marathon Heater (India) Private Limited in Fiscal 2025.
Significant concentration of manufacturing units at Udaipur, Rajasthan, India (10 of 15 units), exposing operations to location-specific disruptions.
Dependence on Projects/OEM business, which contributed 67.55%, 69.16% and 63.99% of revenue from operations (excluding scrap sale and export incentive) for Fiscals 2026, 2025 and 2024 respectively.
Dependence on a relatively limited group of suppliers for key raw materials, with an absence of definitive supply agreements.

Reliance on Subsidiaries / Joint Ventures for international market entry and product launches, with the ability to control and respond swiftly constrained by majority, unanimous or partner consent requirements on key business actions.
Capital-intensive business with substantial capital expenditure and working capital requirements; Net Working Capital Days rose to 210 in Fiscal 2026 from 193 in Fiscal 2025 and 152 in Fiscal 2024.

Goodwill of INR 1,061.28 million recognised from the Marathon Heater amalgamation as at March 31, 2025 is described as a one-time event that may not be repeated and may not be comparable in future periods.

overview.business_model: Sells customised, engineered-to-order thermal and cable products across three verticals — temperature sensing solutions, electrical heating solutions and specialised cables — to industrial customers in metal, petrochemical, defence and nuclear, power, glass and plastics end-markets. Revenue splits between Projects/OEM orders (large, often one-time installations or upgrades: 67.55%, 69.16% and 63.99% of revenue from operations excluding other operating revenue in Fiscals 2026, 2025 and 2024) and MRO/replacement supply of cables and sensors (32.45%, 30.84% and 36.01% for the same periods). Revenue from operations excluding other operating revenue was ₹4,411.04 million in Fiscal 2026 (this RHP prints amounts in ₹ million); other operating revenue (scrap sales and export incentive) was ₹37.74 million in Fiscal 2026. Operations extend through overseas subsidiaries and joint ventures (Tempsens Gulf LLC, Tempsens Instruments GmbH, Tempsens Polska sp. z o.o., PT. Tempsens Asia Jaya, Tempsens Korea Co. Ltd., Tempsens Mexico S.A. de C.V.).

No monitoring agency, no appraisal, and capacity adds of just 7.56% and 11.76%.

parameter_scores.parameter: Disclosure completeness of the offer document

red_flags: The single largest quantified legal exposure in the document sits inside an acquisition completed four months before filing: Theia New Consultancy LLP has sought interim relief of ₹110.41 million before the High Court of Bombay against subsidiary Tempsens Measurement and Control Private Limited (acquired 30 March 2026), alleging breach of the non-solicitation and confidentiality covenants of a 11 March 2022 MOU by channelling a customer's business through a firm controlled by family members of the subsidiary's own directors. The Company's entire other litigation aggregate against it is ₹18.02 million.

The whole Offer for Sale of 18,500,000 shares comes from near-zero-cost holders — Chandra Prakash Talesara at 'Nil', Ankit Talesara ₹0.04, Amit and Puneet Talesara ₹0.05, Nirmal Kumar Pande ₹0.06 per share — while the two Promoters carrying genuine cost (₹55.63 and ₹37.43) sell nothing, and Ankit Talesara is simultaneously a Non-Executive Director and a personal guarantor of the bank facilities the Fresh Issue will repay.

50.00% of Tempsens Instruments GmbH was acquired from the Company's own Promoter and Managing Director Vinay Rathi and from Basant Rathi; GmbH had been a top-10 customer of the Company beforehand, so a related-party sale converted an external customer into a consolidated subsidiary in the same Fiscal in which the accounts are presented.

Share count was inflated from 293,331 to 80,666,025 in the fifteen months before filing — a 25-way sub-division of ₹100 face value into ₹4 effective 30 April 2025 followed by a 10:1 bonus on 30 May 2025 — and every cost-of-acquisition figure in the RHP is stated after those adjustments.

Statutory records are missing or wrong: Form 2 for the 12 October 2004 bonus issue of 30,765 shares and Form 32 for the Chairman's original 1990 appointment are untraceable; the MoA subscription sheet recorded 100 shares each where 1 was subscribed; Form INC-28 recorded the NCLT amalgamation order as 20 February 2025 when it is dated 6 February 2025; certain RoC filing challans cannot be located.

Group Companies — including Pyrotech Electronics, Matplat, Pyrotech Technologies and, notably, the Company's own joint ventures PT. Tempsens Asia Jaya and Tempsens Korea — are empowered under their constitutional documents to engage in a similar line of business, and no non-compete agreements have been entered into with any of them or with Promoter Group members.

Regulatory hygiene shows repeated small breaches: certain manufacturing units operated in excess of the capacity permitted under pollution-board consents to operate (revised consents since obtained); delayed TDS/TCS payments in all three Fiscals (3, 22 and 1 instances); delayed RBI overseas-direct-investment filings; the accounting software audit trail was not enabled at database level for the Holding Company and two subsidiaries for FY26; and CARO flags title deeds not in the Company's name for land and building of ₹201.35 million and ₹484.86 million gross carrying value, both mortgaged to lenders.
Fire no-objection certificates held for Units I, II, IV, V and VI are 'temporary', not permanent — including Units IV and VI, the two units receiving the Offer capital expenditure.
strengths_observed: Structural niche the RHP quantifies: per the commissioned Frost & Sullivan report cited in the RHP, the largest manufacturer of contact and non-contact temperature sensors in India by revenue with ~10.5% of the FY26 temperature-sensor segment, and the only Indian manufacturer of non-contact sensors at ~21.3% share. Both figures are F&S's, not independently verifiable from the RHP.

Profit scaled with revenue over three Fiscals as printed: revenue from operations ₹2,748.10 million (FY24) → ₹3,785.26 million (FY25) → ₹4,448.78 million (FY26); PAT ₹409.19 → ₹625.55 → ₹710.67 million; EBITDA margin 21.98% → 25.45% → 24.83%.

Low leverage: total borrowings ₹779.48 million against net worth ₹4,968.89 million as at 31 March 2026 (printed Debt/Equity 0.15x, Debt/EBITDA 0.69x); contingent liabilities ₹17.39 million = 0.35% of net worth; ICRA rating upgraded to [ICRA]A from [ICRA]A- in August 2024 and reaffirmed November 2025.

Export franchise is real and growing: revenue from outside India ₹586.36 million (21.49% of FY24) → ₹1,258.21 million (28.52% of FY26), products delivered to more than 80 countries between 1 April 2023 and 31 March 2026.

Genuinely low concentration for an SME-scale industrial issuer: top-10 customers 18.59% of FY26 revenue (24.74% in FY24), largest supplier (India Trade Link Private Limited) 20.77% of FY26 purchases, and one reportable segment served across metal, petrochemical, power, defence & nuclear, glass and plastics.

Backward integration and qualification barriers the RHP can evidence: alloy melting, hot rolling, MI cable and machining in-house; ASME 'U' Stamp for pressure vessels at Unit-I; NABL ISO/IEC 17025:2017 calibration laboratory; ATEX, IECEx, UL, CE, PESO approvals; 12 granted Indian patents and 39 overseas trademark registrations; R&D team of 83 (10.20% of 814 employees) spending ₹55.56 million in FY26.

Cross-selling is measured, not asserted: ₹2,668.14 million, 59.97% of FY26 revenue from operations, came from customers purchasing across multiple product categories (57.89% FY25, 57.60% FY24); top-20 customers average 10 years of association (range 1–23 years).
The cable line the capex targets is the one already running hot: Unit-IV utilisation 57.07% (FY24) → 71.84% (FY25) → 90.57% (FY26), and Unit-II specialised cable at 96.00% in FY26.

Operating record is clean on the RHP's own negative confirmations: no shutdowns, accidents or fires at manufacturing units, no material warranty claims, bank-guarantee invocations, order cancellations or recalls, no covenant breach or restructuring, and no lost accreditations across FY24–FY26.
